scope: Proposition 3.1 (Coarse information outside a sublinear collar) of the manuscript “Polynomial PEPS approximation of gapped square-grid ground states” (preprints/Polynomial-PEPS-approximation-of-gapped-square-grid-ground-states-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 265 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0b55ba0b87ad0468), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 9. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer N0 ≥ 1 and a constant A0 ≥ 1. There are β < 1, C < ∞, and u0 < ∞ such that the following holds. Let u ≥ u0 and let T be the full ambient lattice sample of a union of at most N0 axis-parallel rectangles, with diam∞ T ≤ A0u. For every physical set E ⊆ Λ satisfying dist∞(E, T) > uβ , one has IΩ(Λ ∩ T : E) ≤ C. The same statement holds for any subset of Λ∩T in its first argument, for rectangles with consistently assigned open or closed sides, and after a common translation of the lattice coordinates.
